name: list_projects
title: List projects
description: The person's online KiCad projects: the ones they own and the ones shared with them, most recently changed first. Each has an id, a name, the person's role (editor or viewer), who owns it and how many documents it holds. Call this first to find the project to work on; every other tool takes the project's id or exact name.

query.description: Only projects whose name or description contains this text (case-insensitive).

name: get_project
title: Get project
description: One project: its documents (schematic sheets and the board, by path, which is what the document parameter of the other tools takes), the person's role, the members it is shared with, and the address that opens it in the web editor.

project.description: Project id or exact name, as listed by list_projects.

name: create_project
title: Create project
description: Start a new, empty online project owned by the person: a project file, one schematic sheet and one board, named after the project. Returns its id and documents. Use it only when the person asks for a new project or design.

name: get_design_guide
title: Design guide
description: House rules for working on a design here, written for you: the owner's schematic drawing rules (wires inside a block, labels only between blocks, horizontal labels, supplies up and ground down, shared rails for decoupling), how to take a design from a prompt to a routed board in stages, how to plan placement and routing for the engines, and how to review a design. Read the relevant topic once before you draw or rearrange a schematic, lay out or route a board, or write a review.

topic.description: Which part to read; all when omitted.

name: render_view
title: Render image
description: A picture of a schematic sheet or of the board as it is right now, drawn the way the editor draws it (KiCad's colours and stroke font). Use it to see layout, readability and placement that lists of coordinates do not show, and to check your own changes after applying them. Without area or refs it shows the whole sheet or board; a schematic sheet is large, so ask for the part you care about to be able to read values and pin names.

document.description: Document path as listed by get_project, or "board".

area.description: The rectangle to show, [x0, y0, x1, y1] in millimetres.

refs.description: Show these components and their surroundings instead of an area.

layers.description: Board only: draw just these layers, for example ["F.Cu", "Edge.Cuts"]. Default: every layer the editor shows by default.

width_px.description: Longest side of the image in pixels (default 1500).

name: read_document
title: Read source
description: A document as KiCad s-expression text, as it stands now: the file's header followed by every item. For reading exact syntax (to write an add_item edit that matches the file, or to inspect something no structured tool reports). Long documents come in parts; pass next_offset back as offset. Prefer list_components, list_nets and get_items for questions about the design, they are far shorter.

document.description: Document path as listed by get_project, or "board".

name: list_changes
title: List changes
description: The changes made to a project through this connection or the person's other connected apps, newest first: an id, the title, what each edit did, the document, when, and whether it has been undone. The id is what undo_changes and redo_changes take.

name: undo_changes
title: Undo a change
description: Take back one apply_changes call: what it added is removed, what it removed comes back, what it moved or edited returns to how it was, and board rules it set are restored. Everyone in the document sees it happen. It is refused, with nothing changed, when somebody has edited one of the same items since, so nobody's newer work is overwritten. Undo the newest change first when undoing several.

change_id.description: The change to undo, as returned by apply_changes or list_changes. Omit for the most recent change to the project that has not been undone.

name: redo_changes
title: Redo a change
description: Put back a change that undo_changes took away, exactly as it was applied (the same items with the same ids, and the board rules it set). Like an undo it is refused, with nothing changed, when somebody has edited one of the same items since.

change_id.description: The undone change to put back, from list_changes. Omit for the change that was undone most recently.

name: list_comments
title: List comments
description: The review comments people have pinned on a schematic sheet or the board: each thread with what it is pinned to (on: a component or item, net: a net), its position in millimetres, author, text, replies and whether it is resolved. Resolved threads are left out unless include_resolved is true.

document.description: Document path as listed by get_project, or "board".

name: add_comment
title: Add comment
description: Pin a comment on a schematic sheet or the board, signed as the person, where everyone in the project sees it: on a component (ref), on a net (net), or at a point (x, y in millimetres). A comment on a component follows the component when it is moved; one on a net highlights the net when opened. Or answer an existing thread with reply_to. Good for review findings the person wants left on the design; do not comment unless asked to.

document.description: Document path as listed by get_project, or "board".

net.description: Pin it on this net, by the name list_nets gives.

reply_to.description: The id of the thread to reply to, from list_comments.

name: resolve_comment
title: Resolve comment
description: Mark a comment thread resolved once what it asked for is done, or reopen it with resolved false.

name: list_checkpoints
title: List checkpoints
description: The named checkpoints of a project (the versions people saved under a name), newest first, with the documents each covers.

name: create_checkpoint
title: Create checkpoint
description: Save a named checkpoint of the project, the way File > Save Checkpoint does in the editor, so the person can find this state in the project's history. A project linked to GitHub with checkpoint pushes turned on pushes it there as well.

name.description: A short name, for example "Before rerouting the USB pair".

name: run_python
title: Run a Python script on the design
description:
Run a Python script that works on the design with the kicad_harness package. This is the cheapest way to do anything that takes more than a couple of edits: one call places parts, wires them, generates parts from datasheets, lays out and routes the board, and returns only what the script prints. The script never sees or writes KiCad file text and you do not compute coordinates: the harness reads pin positions, finds free space, draws the wires and keeps everything on the grid.

Already defined in the script: `project` (the project named in this call), `kh` (the package) and `parts`. Print what you want to read back, or set a variable named `result` (returned as data). Read get_design_guide with topic "python" once for the whole API; the core of it:

sch = project.schematic()            # or project.schematic("power")
sch.place("Device:R", ref="R1", value="10k", near="U1")   # returns the reference; position is chosen when not given
sch.connect("U1.3", "R1.1")         # wire (or matching labels when there is no clear path); pins by number or name: "U1.VDD"
sch.net("GND", "U1.GND", "C1.2")    # power symbol or label on each pin
sch.decouple("U1.VDD", "100n")       # capacitor at a supply pin, to ground
sch.build(parts=[...], nets={...})   # a whole block from a netlist
sch.check()                           # ERC summary
board = project.board(); board.sync(); board.outline(100, 100, 150, 130)
board.autoplace(groups={...}); board.route(); board.check()
part = parts.from_datasheet(url_or_part_number)   # symbol and IPC-7351 footprint from the datasheet's tables
sch.place(part, ref="U2")
parts.find("3.3V LDO SOT-23-5")     # LCSC, Mouser, DigiKey, TI, Analog Devices

Edits appear in the document as they are made, with your cursor on them, so the people in it can follow (set live to false to apply without the pauses). If the script fails, the edits it had made are taken back and the error names the script line, so fix the script and run it again. There is no network or file access inside the script other than through the harness. A script still working after 45 seconds answers with running: true and a run_id while it carries on: collect its result with get_run instead of running it again.

title.description: A few words naming what the script does. It is what the person sees in the list of changes.

live.description: Draw the edits step by step with a moving cursor (default true).

keep_on_error.description: Keep the edits made before a failure instead of taking them back (default false).

timeout_s.description: Time limit in seconds (default 180, at most 400).

name: check_layout
title: Check sheet layout
description: How a schematic sheet reads: every place where something is drawn on top of something else (text over text, text over a symbol, a wire through text or through a symbol, symbols overlapping, a frame cutting through anything), and anything outside the page border or over the title block. Each finding names the two things and where. Run it after drawing or changing a sheet and fix what it finds: autoplace_fields moves references and values, move and move_region move parts and whole blocks, set_page makes the page larger. It also returns the box around everything on the sheet (extent), the usable drawing area and the title block. Optional: within [x0, y0, x1, y1] measures only what lies inside that box; of [refs] measures those parts with the stubs, labels and power symbols on their pins (what a frame around them must contain); wrap [{text, size, width}] breaks notes into lines that fit a width.

document.description: Which sheet: its path or file name.

within.description: Measure only the items wholly inside this box [x0, y0, x1, y1] in mm.

of.description: Measure these parts (references) with what hangs on their pins.

wrap.description: Notes to break into lines no wider than width mm at this text size.

free.description: Find free room for a box of w by h mm, beside the part named in near when given; the answer's free is its top left corner.

limit.description: How many findings to list (40 by default); the counts are always complete.

name: get_run
title: Get run result
description: Wait for a run_python or apply_changes call that was still working when it answered (its answer had running: true and a run_id). Returns that call's result when it is finished, or running: true again with the time so far; then call get_run again. The work goes on by itself in the meantime and the people in the document see the edits arrive.

run_id.description: The run_id from the answer that said running: true.

wait_s.description: How long to wait for it this time, in seconds (default 45, at most 50).

name: get_geometry
title: Get geometry
description: Every part of a schematic sheet or of the board with its position, rotation, box and the position, side and net of each pin or pad, plus the sheet's wires, labels and junctions or the board's outline, in one compact answer. It is what the Python harness (run_python, or kicad_harness on the person's own computer) plans placement and wiring from; for a question about one part, get_component is smaller.

document.description: Which document: its path, or "board" for the board.
